statement: Write a hiring policy, as a markdown document, for a 25-person software startup in Bangalore. It covers how a role is opened and approved, the interview stages, how offers are made and approved, referral bonuses, diversity and fairness rules, how long candidate data is kept, and who owns and reviews the policy.
audience: Employees and hiring managers of a 25-person software startup in Bangalore, plus HR, department heads and the CEO who run and sign off on hiring.
facts: The hiring manager requests the opening; the department head and the CEO both approve before it is posted
Application and CV screen by HR
2 interviews with the team (role skills, then culture and values)
Final round with the department head
The hiring manager and HR propose the salary and job level using our pay bands
The department head approves the offer
The CEO gives the final yes before the offer is sent
Referral bonus of ₹50,000 after the hire completes 3 months
Candidate data is kept for 12 months
The HR lead keeps this policy up to date
The policy is reviewed every 6 months, or sooner if hiring laws change
standards: Plain, clear language that a new employee can follow
Each section states who does what, in order
Every number and name matches the brief and the answers exactly
No invented facts; anything unknown is marked to be confirmed
rules: Use only facts from the brief and the Requester's answers
Write a markdown document, not a website

Sections in order: Purpose and scope, Opening a role and approving it, Interview stages, Making and approving offers, Referral bonus, Diversity and fairness, Candidate data retention, Ownership and review

Interview stages: lists in order the HR CV screen, 30-minute HR call, take-home task or technical round, 2 team interviews (role skills, then culture and values), final round with the department head, reference check, decision

Making and approving offers: the section shows, in order, that the hiring manager and HR propose salary and job level using pay bands, then the department head signs off, then the CEO gives the final yes before the offer is sent
Referral bonus: states a ₹50,000 bonus paid after the referred hire completes 3 months
Diversity and fairness: sets out fair and non-discriminatory hiring rules that apply to every stage
Candidate data retention: states that candidate data is kept for 12 months
Ownership and review: names the HR lead as owner and states review every 6 months or sooner if hiring laws change
